title: observability: propagate request-id & trace context on API surface (streaming, function-calls, OpenAI-compat)
author: Priya Shah
description: Motivation: Streaming and function-calling flows observed noisy/fragmented telemetry in customer environments because request IDs and trace context were not consistently propagated through the OpenAI-compat layer and streaming proxies. This PR standardizes propagation of a single request_id header and W3C traceparent across the public API, streaming endpoints, and OpenAI-compatible wrappers, and adds per-endpoint metric tags and structured log fields. Goals: 1) Ensure a canonical request_id exists for every external request (generated at edge if absent) and is included in logs, metrics, and traces; 2) Propagate W3C traceparent / tracestate from client to backend and downstream services; 3) Add per-route metric tags so cost/latency/err rate breakdowns include API surface (chat/generate/embeddings/function_call); 4) Fix streaming stability regressions caused by missing request context in chunked response paths. Changes: - Add new middleware redwood/api/middleware/requestid.go that creates/validates X-Redwood-Request-Id and preserves incoming traceparent header. - Implement propagation helpers redwood/observability/tracing/propagation.go to normalise trace headers and attach to context. - Thread request_id + trace context through streaming runtime and function-calling execution paths (redwood/api/server/streaming_handler.go, redwood/openai/compat/handler.go). - Emit structured log fields (request_id, route, trace_id, client_id) from core logger (redwood/observability/logging/structured.go) and ensure logs from third-party plugin hooks include the same fields. - Tag per-endpoint metrics in telemetry pipeline and expose a config-driven allowlist for high-cardinality tags (redwood/console/dashboards/metrics_tags.yaml). - Update Python and TypeScript OpenAI-compat SDK shims to forward custom headers during streaming and function call callbacks (redwood-sdk-python/redwood/openai_compat.py, redwood-sdk-typescript/src/compat/streaming.ts). - Docs: docs/observability/request-id.md and docs/release-notes/observability-2026-02.md. Testing: Unit tests for header parsing and middleware (tests/middleware/requestid_test.go), integration tests for streaming with injected traceparent (tests/integration/streaming_trace_test.py), and load tests verifying no throughput regression. Rollout plan: Feature gated behind env var REDWOOD_OBS_REQUESTID=true and rollout via console toggle. Start with internal staging and canary on Dedicated; 48-hour canary monitoring for increased error rates or metric cardinality before global enable. Checklist: - [x] Middleware implementation and helpers - [x] Threading through streaming runtime and function-calls - [x] SDK forwards headers for streaming/callbacks - [x] Structured logs with request_id and trace_id - [x] Per-route metric tags + allowlist - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Docs and release notes Backwards compatibility: Preserves existing header passthrough; if client provides traceparent we continue the trace, otherwise a new trace is started. High-cardinality tags are opt-in via allowlist to avoid metric explosion.

thread request context through streaming runtime and function-calls

ci_summary: e2e: openai-compat - passed (flaky test rerun fixed)
review_comments: Ethan Cole: Nice consolidation. Can you add a short note in the middleware about how we generate stable ids when upstream provides a non-conforming header?
Priya Shah: Reply - added deterministic UUID v5 generation using namespace + client-provided id as fallback; updated docs to call this out
Marta Alvarez: Please ensure per-route metric tags are behind the allowlist by default (we saw metric cardinality regressions in a prior rollout).
Priya Shah: Reply - metrics now use a server-side allowlist and the default config is the conservative set (chat, generate, embeddings). Added telemetry guardrails in telemetry_pipeline.yaml.
Jordan Kim: Observability SIG noted that traces from streaming chunks were losing parent span in some proxy paths. Did you verify the chunked path preserves span context?
Priya Shah: Reply - yes, added integration test that simulates chunked streaming through the compat proxy; traceparent is preserved and span relationships validated.
Ethan Cole: Approved - minor nit about a log message wording (fixed)
release_notes:
- Added API-level request_id propagation and W3C traceparent support across streaming, function-calls, and OpenAI-compat layers.
- Structured logs now include request_id and trace_id for easier observability.
- Per-endpoint metric tags with server-side allowlist to prevent cardinality spikes.
- Feature gated rollout via REDWOOD_OBS_REQUESTID and console toggle.
notes_for_ops: Enable REDWOOD_OBS_REQUESTID in staging and run canary via console toggle. Watch the metric 'telemetry.metric_cardinality.estimated' and per-endpoint error rates for 48 hours. If cardinality increases >10% or error rate increases >0.5% roll back the toggle.
testing_notes: See tests/integration/streaming_trace_test.py for replay harness that asserts traceparent is present on all streamed chunks and function-calls. Load tests showed <2% tail-latency change at 99th percentile with the feature enabled.
user_impact: Invisible to most users; improved telemetry for debugging and perf. Clients that relied on non-standard custom headers should continue to work; recommend moving to X-Redwood-Request-Id or standard traceparent.
